t: Count Pairs of Connectable Servers in a Weighted Tree Network
o: For each server `c`, count pairs `(a,b)` in different subtrees around `c` whose distances to `c` are both divisible by `signalSpeed`. Removing `c` splits the tree into degree-many branches; distances within a branch are independent, so we count, per branch, how many nodes sit at distance ≡ 0 (mod speed), then combine counts pairwise across branches. Example 1 (path graph, speed 1): through node 2, left part has 2 nodes, right has 3 → 6 pairs. With `n ≤ 1000`, an O(n²) DFS-per-node solution passes comfortably.
k: Pairs must lie in different branches of c — multiply branch counts cumulatively.

a.i: Root a DFS at each candidate `c`; for each neighbor subtree count nodes at distance divisible by the speed; combine as Σ cnt_i · (sum of previous counts).
s: For each c, DFS each neighbor subtree collecting the count of nodes with dist % speed == 0.
a.t: O(n²) — a full DFS from each of the n centers
a.sp: O(n) — adjacency list and recursion stack

w: Recursion depth can hit n=1000 — fine in most judges, but convert to iterative DFS in Python if worried. Edge case: leaves have degree 1, so their answer is 0. Follow-up: for large n, rerooting techniques give O(n) total.
